complexity.notes: The condition `s[i+length-1] in s[i:i+length]` is trivially true whenever length > 0 (the character is by construction inside the slice), so it is just an obscure way to write `if length: length -= 1`. Slicing on every check copies the window; with an unbounded alphabet this approach degrades to O(n * k) since each `in` test scans the window, whereas the idiomatic dict/set sliding window stays O(n) regardless of alphabet. Correct and fast enough here only because the ASCII cap bounds the window.
complexity.summary: Sliding window over s: each step drops the leftmost character (decrement length) then greedily extends while the next character is not already in the window s[i:i+length], tracking the max. Each membership test is a linear scan of a copied slice, but since the window can never exceed the fixed printable-ASCII alphabet (95 chars), every scan is O(1), giving O(n) overall with O(1) extra space.
